clinical_safety.purpose: Clinical decision support and retrieval reference; not a substitute for a clinician, local protocols, or emergency services.
clinical_safety.audience_note: Separate lay first aid from clinician-only interventions. Medication lists are not patient-specific prescriptions.
medication_guardrails: Confirm patient identity, age, weight when relevant, allergies, pregnancy status, renal/hepatic function, current medicines, contraindications, and local formulary.
Use current institutional protocols and product labels for exact dosing, preparation, route, monitoring, and contraindications.
Do not delay emergency transport, imaging, reperfusion, CPR, or specialist review to search this knowledge base.
Do not give oral food, drink, or medicines to a person with possible stroke until swallowing safety is assessed.
Medication use in children, pregnancy, older adults, renal impairment, and critical illness requires extra caution and clinician oversight.
clinical_safety.review_status: Draft reference compiled from the sources listed in each file. Must be reviewed and signed off by the institution's clinical lead before clinical deployment.
clinical_safety.jurisdiction_note: Designed as a general reference with India-relevant emergency number context; confirm local emergency numbers, referral pathways, drug availability, and national guidelines.

scope: Hospital stroke assessment and reperfusion pathway

triage.recognition: BE-FAST: sudden Balance loss, Eyes/vision change, Face droop, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency services. Other red flags include sudden severe headache, confusion, numbness, or trouble walking.
immediate_action: Call emergency services immediately; note the last time the person was known to be well.
Do not give food, drink, aspirin or other oral medicines before clinical assessment.
Check breathing and responsiveness; if not breathing normally, begin CPR.
Tell the receiving team about anticoagulants, recent surgery/bleeding, baseline function and symptom timeline.
do_not: Do not wait for symptoms to resolve; transient symptoms also need urgent assessment.
Do not give aspirin before brain imaging excludes haemorrhage.
Do not lower blood pressure rapidly unless directed by the stroke team.

diagnostic_process.name: Stabilize and activate stroke pathway
details: Airway, breathing, circulation; oxygen only if hypoxaemic per local protocol
Record exact last-known-well time, NIH Stroke Scale where trained, vitals and bedside glucose
Establish IV access; obtain bloods without delaying indicated imaging/treatment

diagnostic_process.name: Urgent neuroimaging
details: Non-contrast CT head to distinguish haemorrhage from ischaemia
CT angiography for suspected large-vessel occlusion; perfusion CT/MRI or MRI in selected extended-window cases
Imaging must not delay otherwise-indicated IV thrombolysis in eligible patients

diagnostic_process.name: Eligibility and mimics
details: Check glucose, anticoagulant use, recent surgery/bleeding, seizure, migraine and other mimics
Apply current institutional thrombolysis/thrombectomy checklist and specialist review

diagnostic_process.name: Disposition and prevention
details: Stroke-unit admission; dysphagia screen before oral intake
ECG/telemetry, vascular and cardiac work-up, rehabilitation assessment, secondary prevention plan

treatment_pathways.time_window: Usually within 4.5 hours for standard IV thrombolysis; selected patients may qualify outside this window using advanced imaging and specialist criteria.
interventions: IV tenecteplase or alteplase for eligible patients under the current stroke protocol
Mechanical thrombectomy for selected large-vessel occlusion; some patients qualify up to 24 hours based on clinical/imaging criteria
Avoid routine antithrombotic administration until post-thrombolysis safety imaging/timing requirements are met
Manage anticoagulant reversal, blood pressure and intracranial complications using the relevant protocol

medicines.role: IV thrombolysis option for eligible acute ischaemic stroke patients under current 2026 AHA/ASA guidance and local protocol.
medicines.clinical_use: Clinician-only; eligibility depends on timing, imaging, contraindications and protocol.
medicines.safety: High-risk bleeding medicine. Do not use before haemorrhage is excluded or outside an approved stroke pathway.

medicines.role: Established IV thrombolysis option for eligible acute ischaemic stroke.
medicines.clinical_use: Clinician-only; protocol-based dosing and eligibility checklist required.
medicines.safety: Risk of intracranial and systemic bleeding; specialist oversight required.

medicines.role: May be used for secondary prevention/acute ischaemic stroke after haemorrhage is excluded and timing requirements are met.
medicines.clinical_use: Clinician-directed only after imaging and thrombolysis review.
medicines.safety: Do not give to a suspected stroke patient at home or before imaging; may worsen intracranial bleeding.

medicines.role: Used selectively to meet thrombolysis thresholds or manage hypertensive emergencies.
medicines.clinical_use: Titrated by trained clinicians with frequent BP monitoring.
medicines.safety: Excessive BP reduction can impair cerebral perfusion; use stroke-specific thresholds.

current_medicine_landscape.note: The current AHA/ASA 2026 acute ischaemic stroke guideline names tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (maximum 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg as recommended IV thrombolytic options for eligible adults within 4.5 hours. This is a guideline update, not a market-sales or prescribing-frequency ranking.
commonly_guideline_supported_classes: Tenecteplase or alteplase for eligible IV thrombolysis
Antiplatelet therapy after haemorrhage exclusion and according to timing
Anticoagulant reversal agents for selected haemorrhage cases
